title: Italian Game: Center Attack
line: White opens the center at once with two pawns side by side.

steps.text: The Italian Game: both bishops aim at the pawns beside the kings.
White prepares and pushes the queen pawn. Black takes it.
Take back with the pawn. Now two of your pawns stand side by side in the center.

also.e4e5: Pushing past is the other main line. This lesson takes back with the pawn.

steps.text: Block the check with your bishop. It offers a trade of bishops.

also.b1d2: The knight can block too. This lesson blocks with the bishop.
also.b1c3: That is the sharp Moller Attack, also sound. This lesson blocks with the bishop.

steps.text: Take back with the knight. It comes out to a square where it guards the center.

also.d1d2: The queen can take back too. This lesson brings the knight out.

steps.after: Black strikes at your center pawn with its own.

steps.text: This is Black's usual answer. Left alone, your two pawns could push on and chase the knights away.
Take the pawn that attacks your pawn on e4, so your center does not break up.
steps.after: The knight takes back and sits in the center.

steps.text: Castle. Your king is safe and a rook comes toward the middle.

also.d1b3: The queen move is also played here. This lesson castles first.

steps.after: Your pawn on d4 stands alone, with no pawn beside it. It gives your pieces room, and Black will aim at it.

steps.text: A slip seen often below master level: here Black moved the bishop back instead of giving check. Your pawns are free to move.
Push a center pawn to chase one of the knights.
steps.hint: A pawn that moves one square forward attacks two squares.
steps.after: A knight is pushed back and your other pawn can chase the next one. Engines rate that slip at about two pawns for White.

summary: Two pawns side by side in the center push the knights away. Black must hit back with its own center pawn.
